question: An engineer must perform a software upgrade on a production Cisco Nexus 7000 Series switch. Before the upgrade activity, the requirement is for all ports to be shut down and routing protocols to terminate gracefully. Which feature must be used to meet these requirements?
theory: Cisco NX-OS's Graceful Insertion and Removal (GIR), configured via a Maintenance Mode Profile, is designed exactly for this scenario: before a disruptive upgrade, it gracefully shuts down interfaces and lets routing protocols withdraw the switch from the topology in an orderly way (e.g., raising OSPF/BGP metrics or performing a graceful shutdown) so traffic reroutes elsewhere first, instead of abruptly dropping when the box goes down for maintenance. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 6 — Graceful Insertion and Removal / Maintenance Mode)
